Intent Lab

A plausible proposal still needs permission.

A local checker that classifies proposed agent actions as aligned, misaligned, or insufficient context using text and action/source features.

01 / THE QUESTION

What needed to work?

An agent can propose a plausible action that does not match the request—or lacks permission to execute it.

A local action checker, Qwen-generated plans, separate permission checks, execution receipts, versioned evaluations, and a review queue containing actual proposals.

03 / THE ENGINEERING

The decision behind it.

Treat the model prediction and permission grant as separate inputs. Preserve failed candidates instead of promoting a checker that blocks legitimate work.

  1. 01User intent & proposal
  2. 02Action / source features
  3. 03Alignment classifier
  4. 04Permission check & receipt
  • Built an action checker with aligned, misaligned, and insufficient-context labels.
  • Integrated Qwen-generated plans, separate permission checks, and execution receipts in a browser demo.
  • Used fictional, in-memory email tools for the demo.
  • Collected 36 local Qwen development runs and 72 actual proposals, compared versioned models on frozen synthetic evaluations, and added a queue for independent label review.

04 / THE EVIDENCE

What the work demonstrates.

Saved Qwen3-4B runs expose the proposed action, checker label, permission decision, and receipt. These familiar development rehearsals are not an independent benchmark.

The four recorded local Qwen3-4B rehearsals preserve proposals, checker decisions, permission checks, and mock execution receipts. These familiar scenarios overlap development data; they are not an independent benchmark.

05 / THE BOUNDARIES

What I can stand behind.

Fictional in-memory tools; no real email. Familiar rehearsals overlap development data. Independent label review and broader generalization remain open work.

Building something useful means being precise about what it does, what has been checked, and what still needs to be tested.
